plan.goal: Retrieve a literature-grounded NAD(P)HX repair enzyme family, collect annotated sequences, and return one representative protein sequence consistent with ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase or NADPHX epimerase function in a metal-dependent nicotinamide nucleotide repair context.
assumptions: Because no starting sequence, structure, organism, or scaffold was provided, the plan uses the validated semantic-family retrieval workflow and returns a representative annotated family sequence as the in-silico candidate.

Mg(2+)/metal dependence, ATP or AMP-associated nucleotide handling, NADPHX-related activity, and ligand accessibility will be grounded from literature and GO-supported family annotations rather than de novo structural validation in this minimal tool set.
A representative sequence from a retrieved NAD(P)HX repair enzyme family is an acceptable executable fallback for the requested output protein sequence.

selection_requirements: The returned sequence is taken from the retrieved family FASTA linked to the literature-derived GO term.
The selected candidate is consistent with NAD(P)HX repair activity and metal-ion-dependent enzyme function based on retrieved evidence.
Sequence analysis supports a plausible enzyme-length soluble protein without obvious low-complexity domination.
